quarterly_data.signal: June-quarter detail (CFO Bren Higgins, call): revenue of $3.66 billion was above the $3.575 billion guidance midpoint and rose 7% sequentially and 15% year over year. Gross margin 62.4%, at the upper end of guidance, 'driven by a more favorable services mix than model and manufacturing scale that served as positive offsets to the challenging memory pricing environment and tariff headwinds'. Operating expenses $682 million ($399 million R&D, $283 million SG&A); operating margin 43.7%; non-GAAP net income $1.39 billion; cash flow from operations $906 million and free cash flow $817 million; trailing-12-month free cash flow margin 28%. CEO Rick Wallace: KLA Services delivered $820 million in revenue, up 17% year over year; CFO: 80% of service revenue is contract-based.
quarterly_data.figure: Revenue $3.66B (+7% QoQ, +15% YoY) vs $3.575B guidance midpoint; GM 62.4%; op margin 43.7%; services $820M (+17% YoY)

quarterly_data.signal: September-quarter model detail (CFO Bren Higgins): foundry logic revenue from semiconductor customers forecast at approximately 73% of semiconductor process control systems revenue to semiconductor customers; operating expenses approximately $690 million, expected to grow 'by roughly $15 to 20 million sequentially over the next several quarters'; other income and expense approximately $25 million expense; planning tax rate 14.5%; non-GAAP diluted EPS $1.16 +/- $0.10 on approximately 1.312 billion shares. The business model is 'designed to deliver 40% to 50% incremental operating margin leverage on revenue growth over the long run'. For calendar 2026 foundry logic is 'probably somewhere close to 65-ish%, so I'll call it low to mid-60s' of semi process control systems. Services: new long-term target of 13% to 15% growth, 'right now at the bottom of that range' this year and expected 'towards the higher end of the range as we move into next year'.
quarterly_data.figure: Sept-qtr foundry logic ~73%; opex ~$690M (+$15-20M per quarter); non-GAAP EPS $1.16 +/- $0.10; CY2026 foundry logic low to mid-60s%

quarterly_data.signal: Gross margin and pricing (call): CFO Bren Higgins said 2026 gross margin had been framed at 'in the 62%, plus or minus' and 'if you look at the guidance we provided and expectations for next quarter, we're going to be above that'; he expects KLA to 'move consistent with our 60% to 65% general incremental operate or incremental gross margin models as we move through 2027'. CEO Rick Wallace: 'in general, the input prices have gone up. Customers recognize that'; 'When we bring out new products, that's when new pricing decisions get made. With existing products, it's a little bit more around other ways to where we can share in some of the increased value'. CFO: 'It's pretty hard to go back to your customers after you've taken orders and start to change prices on those orders.'
quarterly_data.figure: 2026 GM framed at ~62% +/-, expected above; 60-65% incremental gross margin model through 2027

quarterly_data.signal: Competition and share (call): CEO Rick Wallace cited 'the 1,600, 1,700 applications engineers that KLA has worldwide' as part of the moat in a 'very high-mix, low-volume market', and said 'whenever there's fair competition and we're allowed to compete, we do quite well'. Asked about the process control competitive environment: 'No change ... We're definitely seeing positive momentum in markets where we've held last year, like E-beam' and 'we don't see anything to support the idea that we're anything but net share gainers in process control over the foreseeable future'; 'When we're 6x our nearest rival ...'. CFO Bren Higgins: 'We've gained share at a time where a number of our competitors have been able to ship into fabs in China that we haven't been able to ship into.'
quarterly_data.figure: 1,600-1,700 applications engineers; KLA '6x our nearest rival'

quarterly_data.signal: 2030 target model and the 2027 view (call): CFO Bren Higgins said the Investor Day model had semiconductor revenue 'at 11% and wafer equipment at 12%', and 'KLA share of that overall market would grow 150 basis points plus or minus 25 basis points from where we are in 2025'. CEO Rick Wallace: 'If you have more capital required, then we would exceed the model that we laid out for 2030', but 'we're in no position to reset anything as it pertains to 2030'. On 2027 demand: 'I have very few concerns about what's going to happen in 2027. It's pretty clear that the build-out continues.' CFO: legacy customers' role in high-performance computing is not modeled and 'potentially could be an upside factor, although not a big one for us'; on long-lead material 'I'm willing to make bets from an inventory point of view to ensure I'm in a position to support what customers might need.'
quarterly_data.figure: 2030 model: KLA share +150bps +/- 25bps vs 2025; semi revenue 11%, wafer equipment 12%
